_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Sierra Leone covering indigenous Temne and Mende peoples, Province of Freedom, Freetown settlement, Krio culture, British colony and protectorate, Hut Tax War, independence, RUF civil war (blood diamonds), Ebola crisis, and post-conflict recovery.

ethnic_groups.name: Mende

ethnic_groups.name: Limba
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern; among oldest inhabitants; Tonkolili and Bombali districts

ethnic_groups.name: Kono

ethnic_groups.name: Fula/Fulani

ethnic_groups.name: Loko

ethnic_groups.name: Susu

ethnic_groups.name: Sherbro

ethnic_groups.name: Kissi

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Vai, Kuranko, Yalunka, Lebanese)

country_profile.notes_unique: Freetown was founded in 1787 as a settlement for freed slaves; the country supplied many of the first Western-educated Africans; rich in diamonds that fuelled a brutal civil war (1991–2002).

natural_resources.notes: Rich in diamonds (Sierra Leone Selection Trust historic mine; Koidu mine); world's largest rutile deposits (Sembehun/Sierra Rutile); Tonkolili iron ore (closed); Marampa iron ore; alluvial diamond mining (blood diamonds fuelled civil war); Atlantic fisheries.

military.notes: Republic of Sierra Leone Armed Forces (RSLAF); rebuilt by UK International Military Advisory and Training Team (IMATT) after civil war; Kamajor militia (civil defence) disbanded; UN peacekeeping contributor.

infrastructure.notes: Orange, Africell telecoms; poor roads; no functioning railway; Lungi-Freetown crossing challenge.

climate_zones: Tropical monsoon (one of the wettest places on the West African coast)

debt_aid.notes: Heavily aid-dependent; HIPC/MDRI debt relief; economy devastated by civil war (1991-2002) then Ebola (2014-16); iron ore price collapse; IMF ECF programme; Le (leone) has depreciated significantly.

top_universities: Fourah Bay College (1827, oldest university in West Africa)
education.notes: Fourah Bay College ('Athens of West Africa') trained elites across British West Africa; Free Quality School Education (FQSE) 2018; civil war destroyed 1,270+ schools; low female secondary enrollment; teacher motivation issues.

diaspora_migration.notes: Civil war created massive diaspora (especially UK, US); Krio community globally dispersed; returnees contribute to reconstruction; diaspora engagement strategy launched.

digital_economy.notes: ACE submarine cable; Africell and Orange SL primary operators; Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI) driving government tech adoption; open data initiative; low broadband penetration.

country_profile.national_anthem: High We Exalt Thee, Realm of the Free

geography.terrain: Coastal mangrove swamps; wooded hill country; upland plateau; mountains in northeast; beaches
geography.notes: Named 'Lion Mountains' by Portuguese; Freetown—founded 1792 for freed slaves; diamonds (blood diamonds/conflict); Ebola 2014-16; Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary.

economy_extended.notes: Diamonds (Kimberley Process); iron ore (Marampa); rutile/bauxite; agriculture-based; post-civil war/Ebola recovery; high inflation (40%+); new leone redenomination (2022).

health.notes: Ebola outbreak 2014-16 devastated health system (nearly 4000 deaths); Free Health Care Initiative (2010, pregnant women/children under 5); among world's worst physician ratios.

food_agriculture.notes: Rice is staple but deficit; palm oil production; subsistence farming dominates; inland valley swamp rice cultivation.

energy.notes: Bumbuna hydroelectric dam; EDSA/EGTC utilities; extremely low access (especially rural); Turkey Karpowership (floating power); solar expanding.

transport.notes: Lungi airport across estuary (ferry/water taxi/hovercraft to Freetown); limited road network; no railway (dismantled).

tourism.notes: Beautiful beaches; limited infrastructure; Ebola/conflict legacy; ecotourism potential; Bunce Island slave history; Krio heritage.

human_rights_gender.notes: Abolished death penalty (2021, landmark); FGM very prevalent (Bondo society); Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment Act (2022, 30% quota); 2023 election disputed.

security_stability.notes: Post-civil war (1991-2002) recovery; UNAMSIL peacekeeping success; Special Court for Sierra Leone (Charles Taylor trial); relatively peaceful since; August 2023 election tensions.

music_art_traditions: Palm wine music (S.E. Rogie, Ebenezer Calendar)
cultural_heritage.film_industry: Minimal (Blood Diamond filmed about Sierra Leone)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: SLBC state; Awareness Times; Concord Times; Politico; limited but diverse press
cultural_heritage.notes: Krio (Creole) culture from freed slaves; cotton tree symbol; Bunce Island slave fort; diamond history; palm wine music tradition; secret societies.

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law and customary law
legal_system.sharia_applicability: None (small Muslim population uses informal Sharia for personal matters)
legal_system.customary_law_role: Chiefs and customary courts significant in rural areas (Local Courts Act)
legal_system.notes: Special Court for Sierra Leone (2002-13, hybrid UN/national court); Truth and Reconciliation Commission; dual legal system (formal + customary).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.

910.name: Indigenous Peoples of Sierra Leone
910.description: Early settlement by Temne, Mende, Limba, and other groups; rice cultivation; ironworking; Poro and Sande societies.

sub_clusters.name: Early Settlement and Iron Age
sub_clusters.description: Archaeological evidence of early habitation; stone tools; transition to ironworking cultures.

sub_clusters.name: Temne and Mende Formation
sub_clusters.description: Temne settle coastal areas; Mende migrate from interior; decentralised chieftaincies; secret society governance.

920.name: European Coastal Contact and Trade
920.description: Portuguese name 'Sierra Lyoa' (Lion Mountains); early European trade; coastal exchange networks.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Naming and Early Trade
sub_clusters.description: Pedro de Sintra names the peninsula 'Serra Leoa' c.1462; trade in ivory, camwood, and later captives.

sub_clusters.name: European Coastal Trade Networks
sub_clusters.description: English, Dutch, and French traders establish factories; inland trade routes develop; firearms spread.

930.name: Province of Freedom and Freetown Settlement
930.description: Granville Sharp's Province of Freedom; Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia; Maroons from Jamaica; founding of Freetown.

sub_clusters.name: Province of Freedom
sub_clusters.description: Granville Sharp settles 'Black Poor' from London on Sierra Leone peninsula; settlement fails within years.

sub_clusters.name: Nova Scotian Black Loyalist Settlers
sub_clusters.description: ~1,200 Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia re-found Freetown 1792 under Sierra Leone Company; Thomas Peters.

sub_clusters.name: Jamaican Maroon Settlers
sub_clusters.description: ~550 Trelawny Maroons deported from Jamaica via Nova Scotia arrive in Freetown; reinforce settler community.

930.name: Slave Trade and Abolition in Sierra Leone
930.description: Sierra Leone as source and later as destination for recaptured enslaved Africans after British abolition.

sub_clusters.name: Slave Trade from Sierra Leone
sub_clusters.description: Bunce Island slave castle exports captives to Americas, especially South Carolina rice plantations.

sub_clusters.name: Liberated (Recaptive) Africans
sub_clusters.description: Royal Navy's Anti-Slavery Squadron brings ~70,000 recaptured Africans to Freetown; diverse origins form Krio identity.

940.name: British Crown Colony and Protectorate
940.description: Crown Colony from 1808; Krio elite in Freetown; Protectorate over interior 1896; Hut Tax War; two-tier colonial system.

sub_clusters.name: Crown Colony and Krio Society
sub_clusters.description: Freetown as Crown Colony; Krio community develops as educated elite; Fourah Bay College (1827) as 'Athens of West Africa'.

sub_clusters.name: Protectorate Declaration and Hut Tax War
sub_clusters.description: British declare Protectorate over interior 1896; Hut Tax imposed; Bai Bureh leads Temne-Mende uprising 1898.

sub_clusters.name: Late Colonial Period
sub_clusters.description: Mining economy (diamonds, iron ore); SLPP and political development; interior-colony tensions; path to independence.

950.name: Independence and Early Republic
950.description: Independence 1961; Milton Margai; Siaka Stevens' APC one-party state; economic decline.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Sierra Leone
sub_clusters.description: Sierra Leone independent 27 April 1961; Milton Margai PM; SLPP government; diamond economy.

sub_clusters.name: Siaka Stevens and APC One-Party Rule
sub_clusters.description: Stevens seizes power through coups and elections; one-party state 1978; patronage politics; economic collapse.

sub_clusters.name: Joseph Momoh and State Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Momoh succeeds Stevens; deepening economic crisis; state institutions decay; conditions for civil war.

960.name: Sierra Leone Civil War (RUF)
960.description: Revolutionary United Front (RUF) insurgency backed by Charles Taylor; blood diamonds; ECOMOG and British intervention; Special Court.

sub_clusters.name: RUF Insurgency and Blood Diamonds
sub_clusters.description: Foday Sankoh's RUF invades from Liberia; amputation campaigns; 'blood diamonds' fund war; ~70,000 killed.

sub_clusters.name: ECOMOG and British Intervention
sub_clusters.description: ECOMOG restores Kabbah government; British Operation Palliser 2000; UN UNAMSIL; Lomé Peace Accord.

sub_clusters.name: Special Court for Sierra Leone
sub_clusters.description: Hybrid court tries war crimes; Charles Taylor convicted; Hinga Norman, Fofana, Kondewa cases.

960.name: Post-Conflict Sierra Leone
960.description: Post-war reconstruction; democratic elections; Ebola crisis; mudslide disasters; ongoing development challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Post-War Reconstruction
sub_clusters.description: DDR programmes; Truth and Reconciliation Commission; Koroma and Bai presidency; diamond governance reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Ebola Crisis in Sierra Leone
sub_clusters.description: West African Ebola epidemic kills ~4,000 in Sierra Leone; health system overwhelmed; international response.

sub_clusters.name: Contemporary Sierra Leone
sub_clusters.description: Julius Maada Bio presidency (SLPP); education reforms; contested 2023 elections; economic challenges.
